clue.text: Old vice president has not paid for underground movement

parts.note: Aaron Burr was an early US vice president
someone who has not paid is still owing

explanation.surface: A former vice president has skipped a payment for a resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground movement' suggests a resistance group, but here it is literal: digging through the earth like a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunnelling through soil, as rabbits or moles do, is literally a movement underground.

clue.text: New wife for Irish saint

definitions.meaning: St ..., also called Brigid, a patron saint of Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: A woman on her wedding day is so called, and it is also the name of the Irish saint Brigid.

clue.text: Red tape in new form — superficially new

indicators.note: putting these words in a new form means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Bureaucracy rebranded is only cosmetically new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder: RED TAPE IN gives nine letters for the nine-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh coat of paint makes something look new on the surface only.

clue.text: Nuts in a restaurant?

definitions.meaning: slang for crazy or not all there
literally away from the office having a midday meal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mad, and read literally it describes someone away eating their midday meal.

clue.text: Fast and loose she ain't

indicators.note: letters set loose are free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that she is no loose woman, not fast at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast and loose' looks like a single idiom; 'Fast' is the definition and 'loose' scrambles SHE AIN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something quickly and hurriedly is doing it fast.

clue.text: Boy making girl eat cheese

indicators.note: the girl's word takes the cheese inside her, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A lad gets a girl to eat some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, as borne for instance by Gabriel Oak or the archangel.

clue.text: Press release about some predictions?

indicators.note: turned about, so the run is read backwards
only some of the word predictions is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A press release concerning a few forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press release' sounds like PR, but it is the drink released from an apple press; the run REDIC inside 'predictions' is turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: This drink is the juice that a fruit press releases from crushed apples, then fermented.

clue.text: Mineral associated with cold heart

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A rock associated with a cold heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The central part of something, such as an apple, is its heart.

clue.text: Doctor needing a doctor for practice

parts.note: someone ill needs medical help

explanation.surface: A GP who is unwell and needs to see a colleague at the surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like a medical practice, but it means repeated exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetitive training exercises, as soldiers do on the parade ground, are practice.

clue.text: Apostates making Greene sad

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Lapsed believers upsetting Graham Greene, the Catholic novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who desert their faith or cause are apostates, turncoats.

clue.text: Fashionable place making contribution

parts.note: in means fashionable, in vogue
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A trendy spot that makes a donation.
explanation.definitionFit: What someone contributes to a discussion or project is their input.

clue.text: One book accepted by Henri, translated by an Irishman

indicators.note: Henri takes the other letters in among his own
a translation puts the letters into a different order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Henri renders a book into English for an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henri' is fodder, not the man: put I and B into HENRI, rearrange to HIBERNI, then add AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so a native of it is an Irishman.

clue.text: This period is for composition in a newspaper office

definitions.text: This period is for composition in a newspaper office

indicators.note: a composition puts letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A stint spent writing at a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an anagram of THIS PERIOD gives the time spent in charge of a paper's composition.
explanation.definitionFit: The term during which someone is a newspaper's editor is their tenure in that office.

clue.text: Hit a pest

definitions.meaning: a garden mollusc that eats plants

explanation.definitionFit: To punch someone is to strike them, and the slimy garden creature is a pest to gardeners.

clue.text: Conclusive evidence to terminate the hearing

parts.note: a sound argument is one that is conclusive
proof is evidence that establishes a fact

explanation.surface: Decisive evidence brought to end a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session but means the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulating a room so no noise passes stops anyone hearing what goes on.

clue.text: Iceberg possibly seen by Balt leads to utter chaos eventually

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian, one of the Baltic peoples

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An iceberg sighted by a Baltic sailor ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iceberg' suggests a Titanic scene, but it is a salad variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is one variety of the salad leaf, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: A bit of fun with players in bloomers

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun
Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football team

explanation.surface: Some fun with actors in Victorian underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests knickers; here it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: These delphinium-like flowers are plants that bloom, hence bloomers.

clue.text: House on reclaimed land abandoned by queen and king

parts.note: Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac

indicators.note: the queen leaves, so her letters drop out

parts.note: a polder is low land reclaimed from the sea, as in the Netherlands
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A Dutch house on reclaimed land left behind by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Belgian monarchs bore this name, so it names a king.

clue.text: Start eating, or I get into mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A mess-hall call to begin eating, as I tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into' is only a link; EATING and OR I together are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to originate it, bring it into being.

clue.text: In the German retreat, Mussolini needed to be cut down

indicators.note: Mussolini's title goes in the middle
a retreat goes backwards, so the German word is reversed

parts.note: der is German for the
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: Mussolini had to be cut down during the German withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reduced has been cut down in size or amount.

clue.text: Irish house that is beginning to sell papers

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: only the beginning of the next word

explanation.surface: The Irish parliament starting to sell newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily newspapers are papers, collectively called dailies.

clue.text: Cakes ordered in cafés

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Cakes ordered in cafes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing an order at the counter, but it rearranges IN CAFES.
explanation.definitionFit: Small iced cakes are called fancies, as in French fancies.

clue.text: Head of government in the end will reveal swindle

indicators.note: the head letter goes into the end

parts.note: the finale is the end of a show

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The prime minister will finally expose a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To finagle is to obtain by trickery, so to swindle.

clue.text: Place for notice

definitions.meaning: to see or catch sight of

explanation.definitionFit: A location is a spot, and to notice something is to spot it.

clue.text: King beginning to lay waste

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, in England

indicators.note: only the beginning of the next word

explanation.surface: A monarch starting to lay the land waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is animal entrails, often treated as waste parts of a carcass.

clue.text: Criminal act of fool being dozy?

parts.note: to kid is to fool someone
napping is dozing

explanation.surface: Is fooling while half-asleep a crime?
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction of a person is a serious crime.

clue.text: Sum of money provided for piano?

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
a large concert piano, as opposed to an upright

explanation.definitionFit: A thousand pounds is slang for this word, and a large concert piano is called by it too.

clue.text: Plant's half-life — 50 years

indicators.note: only half the word, its first two letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A plant's half-life measured over fifty years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-life' suggests radioactivity; the hyphen hides the halving indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering bulb plant, such as the Madonna variety.

clue.text: Constant fun — getting tipsy and being sick

indicators.note: a tipsy word staggers, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: ailing means being sick

explanation.surface: Endless fun of getting drunk and throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never fails is steady and constant.

clue.text: Contender for top American office job, amazingly constrained

indicators.note: the run is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A presidential hopeful's job, amazingly tightly held.
explanation.definitionFit: He ran for US president, the top American office, in 2008.

clue.text: Yorkshire town with odd bits of steel in reserve …

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters only

parts.note: put by means kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A northern town with steel set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Selby is a market town in North Yorkshire, known for its abbey.

clue.text: … town that produced steel before Wednesday

definitions.text: town that produced steel before Wednesday

parts.words: town that produced steel before Wednesday
parts.note: a famous steelmaking city whose name comes before Wednesday in a football club's title

explanation.surface: A town that made steel before midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club; the city was famed for steel.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Yorkshire city was the great centre of British steel and cutlery.
